2.text: of the body are laid one or two long sticks to serve as legs in the land of

3.text: the dead.¹ Sometimes the sticks are placed apart, or even near the head

4.text: of the corpse. These sticks are not necessarily taken from the house-frame.

5.text: Since wood is scarce, the people take it wherever they find suitable material.

6.text: The antlers are begged or bought from the nearest reindeer-breeders, and

7.text: those of wild reindeer killed on the hunt are also used.

8.text: All corpses are exposed on the same place by the whole village, so

9.text: that a kind of cemetery is formed. Broad and even mountain-slopes are

10.text: selected for this in some villages; while in others, on the contrary, the funeral

11.text: place is chosen on the very shore, near the water. To give an illustration,

12.text: the dead of the village of Uñiˊsak are exposed on the point of the spit,

13.text: about half a mile from the village. The spit is in the form of a low ridge

14.text: sloping on both sides. The continuation of the ridge forms the chief street

15.text: of the village, separating the houses into two groups. This street is considered

16.text: to be the way by which the dead and the spirits go to the village, and

17.text: nobody dares to select a house site on it, so that it remains unoccupied all

19.text: In winter the corpses are taken to the funeral place on a sledge drawn

20.text: by dogs or by the house-mates of the dead. In summer they are carried

21.text: suspended from the pole which is to be left with the body, being firmly

22.text: tied to it, the face directed towards the pole. The carriers of the corpse

23.text: often change places, or are replaced by others, evidently for the purpose of

24.text: circumventing the deceased in the case of pursuit. On reaching the spot,

25.text: the pole is untied, and deposited in its usual place, near the feet of the

26.text: corpse. In other cases the body is tied all around with thong, three pairs

27.text: of loops being left on each end, by which the “followers” carry it. A dog

28.text: is killed on the funeral place, and the guts are drawn out and laid on the

30.text: All kinds of sacrifices are given to the dead. I found scattered every-

31.text: where on the funeral places, besides dry bones and skulls, heaps of antlers,

32.text: broken rifles, empty brandy-bottles, playing-cards, etc. Kuvaˊr, a trader of

33.text: Uñiˊsak, whose name has been mentioned several times, left on the funeral

34.text: place of one of his sons even a graphophone and an old whaling-boat. All

35.text: these objects were also broken. Here evidently there was no fear of theft.
